seven_day_history.title: Model Boundaries Need Tests That Vary the Context
seven_day_history.summary: A controlled pay-stub editing study probes how context changes model responses. It supports a focused application test, while its simulated setting limits conclusions about real-world outcomes or overall ethics.

sources.title: How Firm Are AI Models’ Ethical Boundaries? A pay-stub editing test of 15 models

seven_day_history.title: Catalog Fields Need Different Checks for Evidence
seven_day_history.summary: An experiment on museum records separates field coverage from support for a generated claim. It offers a focused test pattern for teams generating descriptions from structured data.

sources.title: When More Metadata Misleads: Probing Field-Level Grounding in LLM-Generated Museum Descriptions, v1
sources.publisher: arXiv · Clemencia Siro and Laura Hollink

seven_day_history.title: The Best Ticket-Routing Decision May Be to Defer
seven_day_history.summary: A cost-aware IT-routing study makes human triage an explicit option. Its results favor evaluating the whole decision policy, including the cost of a wrong route and the capacity of the review queue.

sources.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification

seven_day_history.title: Compound Policies Need Inspectable Decisions
seven_day_history.summary: SCOPE explores compiling natural-language policies into smaller predicates and explicit logic. The enterprise opportunity is a policy decision whose components can be tested, explained, and maintained separately.

sources.title: SCOPE — compiling natural-language policies into neurosymbolic predicate programs

seven_day_history.title: Evaluation Scores Need Their Prompts and Judges Attached
seven_day_history.summary: Two new studies show how wording, tool interfaces, judge choice, and language affect model comparisons. An enterprise scorecard needs to preserve those conditions and expose important reversals.

sources.title: Prompt Sensitivity in Tool-Augmented Model Comparisons
Prompting Strategy Effects Depend on the Judge: A Multilingual Study of LLM-as-a-Judge Robustness
